statement: What value of $x$ satisfies the equation $\sqrt{2x - 3} + 5 = 12$?

choices.misconception: I set $2x - 3$ equal to $7$ without squaring, so I solved $2x = 10$ and got $x = 5$.
I isolated the root and squared to get $2x - 3 = 49$, but then I subtracted $3$ instead of adding it, so I had $2x = 46$.
I squared both sides before isolating the root and treated the square of the left side as $2x - 3 + 5$, so I solved $2x + 2 = 144$.

hints: Get the square root by itself before you square anything.
Subtract $5$ from both sides, square both sides, then solve the linear equation. Check your answer in the original.

solutions.reliable: Subtract $5$ from both sides: $\sqrt{2x - 3} = 7$. Square both sides: $2x - 3 = 49$, so $2x = 52$ and $x = 26$. Check: $\sqrt{2(26) - 3} + 5 = \sqrt{49} + 5 = 7 + 5 = 12$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
